events.credibility_reason: The paper's verified content is a bisection-width bound for 3-regular Ramanujan graphs; its transfer to a 0.082n pathwidth lower bound rests only on a search snippet, and the attribution is disputed.

why: All three events are dated before 26 January 2024. Fomin–Høie (2006) and Bezrukov et al. (2000, conference version) are pre-snapshot by year. Bachtler–Heinrich's first public argument is arXiv v1 of October 2020, and the 2024 JGT deposit shows no new mathematics (F1). Fomin–Høie bounds M(n) above by (1/6+ε)n and leaves the quantity open, so it is a bound published in a journal of record. Bezrukov et al. bound bisection width. That gives a pathwidth lower bound only through a transfer that the record could not confirm, so I score it a bound and mark it doubtful. Bachtler–Heinrich relates girth to pathwidth and does not move M(n) as a function of n, so its scope is none. Its finite extremal tables are not witnesses for the statement. No event involves AI. No pre-snapshot event resolves the question either.
doubts: Neither primary text for Fomin–Høie nor for Bezrukov et al. was read. The exact constants and the attribution of 0.082n rest on Wikipedia and on search snippets. The post-2024 citation search could not be run, so a later improvement in a paper that does not use the problem's wording could have been missed.
